hook.text: When children grow up speaking a pidgin, they transform it—adding grammar, complexity, and depth.

buildup.text: A creole is a pidgin that became a native language—acquired by children as their first tongue.

discovery.text: Haitian Creole, Tok Pisin, and Jamaican Patois are fully expressive creole languages.

twist.text: Children don't just learn the pidgin—they expand it, adding tense, aspect, and complex clauses.

climax.text: This suggests children have an innate drive to create complex grammar even from minimal input.

punchline.text: Give children a pidgin and they'll build a full language.

quiz.question: How does a creole differ from a pidgin?
options: A creole has native speakers and full grammar
